notes.text: Anthony Mantha is out and missed their last game.
Kirill Marchenko is on injured reserve and has missed the last 4 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.

Nick Blankenburg is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 6 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Troy Stecher has taken his spot beside Oliver Ekman-Larsson. That pair has had 57% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 32:14 together, up from 48% with Blankenburg.
Max Domi is on long-term injured reserve and has not played this season.
Morgan Rielly is out (lower-body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-pair defenseman.
John Tavares returned in their last game after missing 9 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Oliver Ekman-Larsson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 29% of the team’s shorthanded time in 18 games, up from 6% last season.

stakes: The Devils go in second in the Metropolitan with 24 points, the Maple Leafs seventh in the Atlantic with 18 points.

TOR.head: The Maple Leafs have a hill to climb
TOR.body: Even though Toronto has home-ice advantage, New Jersey has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Toronto will be without Marchenko. The Maple Leafs’ best way through is keeping dangerous shots away.

story.head: The Devils are on a heater
paras: The Maple Leafs (8-8-2) lost 4-2 to Montréal last night, while the Devils have won four straight. Going in, the Devils are second in the Metropolitan (tied for sixth in the NHL) and the Leafs seventh in the Atlantic (tied for 19th).

The Devils have played better than their record (.706) says: their chances are worth about .764, and their goaltending has held them back. The Maple Leafs’ record (.500) is about what their chances are worth.

The Devils rarely throw hits (3rd lowest) and keep things calm after the whistle (3rd lowest). They also throw more pucks at the net than almost anyone (3rd), so the Devils are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Maple Leafs. On the other side, the Maple Leafs get their shots through better than anyone (1st), but take more penalties than they draw (31st) and take a lot of low-quality shots (31st). Both teams like to play fast, so expect an open game.

Jack Hughes (9 G / 14 A / 23 P in 17 GP) is carrying the Devils’ offense, with nine points in his last five games and six goals in seven games against Toronto since 2023-24. Auston Matthews (11 G / 16 A / 27 P in 18 GP) leads the Maple Leafs in scoring and is sixth in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games and seven goals in eight games against New Jersey since 2023-24. William Nylander (11 G / 11 A / 22 P in 18 GP) is next in line.
Jake Allen (6-3-0 / .881 SV% in 9 GS) is expected to go for New Jersey. Anthony Stolarz (5-1-0 / .910 SV% in 6 GS) has been outstanding for Toronto and is expected to start.
The Devils usually control more of the chances than the Maple Leafs do.
